title: PeerHttpClient::new() uses WebPKI but kithd presents self-signed certs
description:
Trigger: any production kithd-to-kithd delivery attempt. kithd generates a self-signed cert via rcgen (load_or_generate_cert). PeerHttpClient::new() (used by outbox_worker in main.rs) builds a hyper HTTPS client with .with_webpki_roots(). WebPKI roots include only publicly trusted CAs (Mozilla bundle); a self-signed cert is not among them. Every outbound Peer/deliver call fails with a TLS error. Messages remain stuck in 'pending' state indefinitely.

The blob-fetch path (fetch_peer_blob) correctly uses TailnetCertVerifier (accepts any cert from a tailnet IP). The discovery probe (probe_peer) also uses TailnetCertVerifier. Only the delivery path uses WebPKI, creating an inconsistent and broken TLS policy.

Fix options: (a) use TailnetCertVerifier for PeerHttpClient, matching the blob-fetch and discovery paths; (b) integrate with 'tailscale cert' to obtain a WebPKI-trusted cert; (c) document that users must supply a WebPKI-trusted cert before production use. Option (a) is lowest friction given Tailscale's network-layer identity guarantee.
